clue.text: Run in wrong way — like this?

indicators.note: in places the run's letter inside the scrambled word
wrong tells us the letters of the word way are set out in a wrong order

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone running the wrong way along a track wonders whether this is what going astray looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns WAY into AWY and 'in' puts R inside it. The definition 'like this?' is self-referential: the answer sits in the grid like everything else, yet means askew.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done askew or off course has gone amiss, which the question 'like this?' points at after a run gone wrong.

clue.text: Do what you need here — and everywhere else

definitions.text: Do what you need here — and everywhere else

parts.words: Do what you need here — and everywhere else
parts.note: the solver's task in every light of the grid is to write in the solution, and this light names that task

explanation.surface: An instruction telling someone to do what is required here and in every other place.
explanation.walkthrough: Part of the self-reference theme: the light names the thing you write into it and into every other light.
explanation.definitionFit: Every entry in a crossword is filled with its solution, so what you need here and everywhere is the reply to the clue.

clue.text: Activity in courts produced by fraudulent schemes

definitions.meaning: a game played with a ball in a walled court, related to squash

explanation.surface: Fraud cases brought before the law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both the walled-court ball game and criminal swindles.

clue.text: Trendy scene indicating 17 in 9, 14, and 29

definitions.meaning: the fashionable place to be, the centre of the action
the lights at 9, 14 and 29 each describe their own position in the grid, a kind of self-reference

explanation.surface: A fashionable venue described with a run of crossword cross-references.
explanation.walkthrough: SECOND ROW sits in the second row, FIFTH COLUMN in the fifth column and BOTTOM LINE on the bottom line, so each tells you its own location.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the fashionable spot and, read literally, a statement of location.

clue.text: Result of tough negotiations as lawyers in firm profit

indicators.note: in places the lawyers inside the joined words for firm and profit

parts.note: firm means hard, unyielding
a profit is a gain
the Bar is the collective name for barristers

explanation.surface: A firm's lawyers squeeze out a profit after tough talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. BAR goes into HARDGAIN, between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal driven by a tough negotiator, with little given away, is the outcome of fierce haggling.

clue.text: Red or green

definitions.meaning: red as in uncooked, bloody meat

explanation.surface: Two colours offered as alternatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncooked meat is red, and an untrained recruit is green; one adjective covers both.

definitions.meaning: allowed off a vehicle, as a passenger is dropped

parts.note: a story is a tale
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An editor puts together a story collection of real accomplishment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts TALE above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplished and gifted are synonyms for someone with natural skill.

clue.text: Earning about a pound is annoying

indicators.note: about means the word for earning goes around the pound

parts.note: earning as net income, netting
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone finds it irritating to earn only about a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEDLING also fits the definition, but the wordplay settles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate someone is to sting them like the stinging plant, so annoying is a synonym.

clue.text: After a little drink, a new driver appears to wreck car, say

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
L is the learner plate shown by a new driver in Britain

explanation.surface: After a quick drink, a learner driver seems to have smashed the car up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just sets the order and 'appears to' is a link. As a verb, to total a car is to write it off completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing off a vehicle completely is informally to total it; 'say' marks a car as one example of what can be destroyed.

clue.text: Newspaper article supporting 20% in treacherous group

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means sitting underneath and holding up the other piece

parts.note: twenty per cent is one fifth
a column is a regular newspaper article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece backs a twenty-per-cent stake in a group of traitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The answer sits in the fifth column of the grid, which is part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sympathisers working secretly inside a country for its enemy are called by this Spanish Civil War phrase.

clue.text: Part of speech, as it is

definitions.text: Part of speech, as it is

parts.words: Part of speech, as it is
parts.note: the answer names a word class and is itself a member of that class, so it describes itself

explanation.surface: A grammar note saying a word is one class of speech, just as it stands.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the self-referential answers listed at 17: a naming word that is itself a naming word.
explanation.definitionFit: A naming word such as cat or table is one grammatical class, and the word for that class belongs to it.

clue.text: Saint including article in foreign language

indicators.note: including means the saint's name takes the article inside it

parts.note: St Francis of Assisi
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A saint's name with an article added gives a language spoken abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The answer is the French word for French, so it is a foreign word naming a foreign language: one of the self-references at 17.
explanation.definitionFit: French is the language of France, foreign to an English solver, and this is its own name for it.

clue.text: As seen in 1 Down, 15, 16, 22, and 30, not an independent testimonial?

definitions.meaning: each of those answers describes itself, such as a naming word that is a naming word
a testimonial written by its own subject rather than an independent referee

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced list ends with doubts about a reference that is not impartial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'independent' also nods at the newspaper the puzzle appeared in.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing your own reference would be the opposite of impartial testimony, and the phrase also means a statement about itself.

clue.text: Terrible weapon, after a short time, dispersed mob repeatedly

indicators.note: after means the scrambled letters come behind the a and the short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: dispersed means the letters are scattered into a new order
repeatedly means the word mob is used twice over

explanation.surface: A dreadful weapon disperses the mob again and again after only a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: MOBMOB, scrambled by 'dispersed', gives OMBOMB, which follows A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear fission bomb is the archetype of a dreadful weapon.

explanation.surface: Reassuring words offered in a serious crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like an adjective meaning serious; it is the burial place, where such words are carved.
explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a tombstone usually speaks well of the dead, so it is complimentary wording on a grave.

definitions.meaning: an aromatic herb used in sauces
a fortune, as in 'it cost a ...'

explanation.surface: A factory that turns out huge sums of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory, fitting 'makes'; it is the herb. 'that makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names an aromatic herb and, informally, a vast sum of money.
